titel: McDonald's CEO on Going Viral, the Big Arch and the Fast-Food Value War

einzeiler: McDonald’s CEO Chris Kempczinski on going viral, value wars, and the Big Arch.
kurzfassung: McDonald's CEO Chris Kempczinski discusses the viral backlash to his Big Arch burger video and how the brand navigates social media. He explains the company's dual strategy of offering premium menu items alongside value deals to appeal to all customer segments. Furthermore, he addresses inflation pressures, franchisee relations, and the growing importance of chicken in their global menu.
stichpunkte: Chris Kempczinski addresses his viral Big Arch tasting video and the online mockery from competitors like Burger King and Wendy's.
McDonald's embraces the creator economy and authentic consumer engagement while avoiding political culture wars.
The brand balances a dual strategy of value deals, such as a new sub-$3 menu, and premium offerings like the Big Arch.
Franchisees face significant cost inflation on labor, packaging, and beef, requiring careful pricing strategies.
Lower-income consumers remain financially stressed by non-discretionary costs like housing, healthcare, and energy.
Scale and strong unit economics allow McDonald's to compete aggressively in the fast-food value war.
A dedicated restaurant experience team focuses on improving food preparation, equipment, and taste perception.
Chicken products are growing faster globally than beef, presenting a major opportunity to boost margins and meet consumer demand.

clips.text: The fast-food giant serves everyone and deliberately stays out of political debates to provide customers with a welcome escape.
Nearly everyone visits McDonald's at least once a year, requiring the menu to cater to all demographics.
A massive daily visitor count generates vast amounts of data that directly inform future menu updates.

clips.hook: How taste perception works before the first bite
clips.text: The majority of a customer's flavor experience is shaped before eating through sourcing, restaurant aromas, and food preparation.

clips.hook: Chicken is twice as big as beef
clips.text: The poultry market is significantly larger and generally cheaper than the beef market, making it a strategic priority.

beschreibung:
When McDonald’s CEO Chris Kempczinski took a small bite out of a big burger on camera, the internet—and his rivals—pounced. But in an era where CEOs are the face of the brand, is there such a thing as bad publicity? In this episode of Bold Names, WSJ’s Tim Higgins sits down with Kempczinski at McDonald's Chicago headquarters to discuss the fallout of his viral moment. Plus, they dive deep into the fast food giant’s strategy to compete by balancing a premium half-pound burger against the urgent need for meal deals in an economy where many customers are concerned with affordability.

To watch the video version of this episode, visit our WSJ Podcasts YouTube channel or the video page of WSJ.com.
